DASH.thesis_one_line: The largest US food-delivery app, now genuinely profitable and beating its own growth guidance, but facing real gig-worker regulatory risk.
kill_criteria: Marketplace GOV YoY growth falls below 20% for two consecutive quarters (36-37% reported includes Deliveroo; ex-Deliveroo Q2-2026 was 23%, and Deliveroo laps in Q4-2026).
Adjusted EBITDA margin (% of GOV) declines YoY for two consecutive quarters
Any final ruling or settlement reclassifying Dashers as employees in California or another large state
Net cash (cash + investments - debt) declines by more than $1B in two consecutive quarters outside a disclosed acquisition
GAAP operating margin below 2% for two consecutive quarters
key_adverse_facts: California EDD assessment (issued Jan 2023) alleges Dashers should be classified as employees; DASH is contesting and has accrued an undisclosed amount (10-Q, Q2-2026, Item legal proceedings)
10-Q discloses ongoing multi-jurisdiction regulatory investigations/audits on Dasher classification, pay models, consumer protection, privacy/cybersecurity, tax and unemployment insurance

Large and persistent GAAP-vs-Adjusted-EBITDA gap (~$758M in Q2-2026 alone), driven mainly by stock-based compensation - GAAP operating margin (3.5-7.5%) is far below the adjusted-EBITDA framing management emphasizes
Secondary sources report a ~$131.5M multi-state worker-payment settlement (NYC/NY/IL/DC) that I could not verify against a primary SEC filing in the time available

Operating margin has been volatile quarter to quarter (3.5% to 7.5% over the last 8 quarters), not steadily improving, due to Deliveroo integration costs and Dasher-incentive/weather items called out by management
DASH.confidence_in_thesis: medium (strong primary-source financial trend; regulatory outcome and durability of the recent buyback/margin trajectory are genuinely uncertain)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: DV12 restatement: SBC is now deducted. After-SBC TTM FCF $1,025M (company FCF $2,139M less SBC $1,114M) at r 11.5% (5.17% + 1.52 x 4.14%), 3% terminal, EV $81.5bn implies about 30%/yr 10-year FCF growth, above the 22% base case and the 24% organic (ex-Deliveroo) revenue growth; the earlier 19-20% added SBC back and was compared with Deliveroo-inflated growth. Verdict INCLUDE-SMALL -> WATCH.

DASH.scenario_basis: DV12 restated: company TTM FCF $2,139M grown 10%/22%/30% a year for 3 years less SBC ($1,114M grown 8%/10%/12%); exit value = year-3 after-SBC FCF x DCF-consistent multiple (r 11.5%, terminal 3%, 7 further years of 7%/18%/24% growth); net cash $3.0B/$5.5B/$6.0B; 439M shares flat (buybacks offset SBC); no dividend. Low-to-medium confidence.

DELL.thesis_one_line: A legacy PC and server maker turned major AI-server integrator with a $95 billion order backlog, priced almost exactly at its own newly raised earnings guidance.
kill_criteria: AI-server backlog declines quarter-over-quarter (vs $95B at Q2 FY2027) for two consecutive quarters
FY2027 non-GAAP EPS guidance is cut from the current $25.50
Core debt (ex-DFS financing, currently ~$24.9B) rises above $30B without proportional ISG operating-income growth
Consolidated operating margin compresses by more than 300 bps YoY in any quarter (most recent quarter 11.5%)

Loss or pause of any single disclosed customer/contract representing more than 10% of ISG revenue (concentration not yet quantified from filings reviewed - criterion to be tightened once segment data is located)
key_adverse_facts: Total consolidated debt is $34.5B, of which $9.6B is DFS (captive-finance) debt tied to customer leases - a real balance-sheet risk if AI-server demand reverses and receivable credit quality deteriorates, distinct from the ~$24.9B of core corporate debt

Guidance has been raised twice within the same fiscal year by very large increments (revenue guide midpoint +15%, EPS guide +42% from Q1 to Q2 FY2027 alone), signalling AI-server order timing is genuinely lumpy and hard to forecast - the same dynamic that produced the upside surprises could produce a downside one

Revenue and backlog growth are concentrated in Nvidia-platform rack integration for a small set of hyperscale/AI customers - a customer loss or a shift to buying direct from ODMs would hit disproportionately
10-Q Item 1 (Legal Proceedings) text could not be fully retrieved in the time available; litigation status is not confirmed clean, only that no material litigation surfaced in web searches
Quarterly (as opposed to annual) operating cash flow could not be fully isolated from cumulative YTD XBRL tags for the two most recent quarters in the time available
H1 FY27 cash conversion fell: operating cash flow $6.3bn vs net income $7.6bn (0.83x vs 1.88x in FY26) and Q2 FCF $986M, down 47% YoY, as receivables and financing receivables built by about $11.8bn.
DELL.confidence_in_thesis: medium (backlog and guidance track record are strong and primary-sourced; customer concentration and DFS financing risk are real and not fully quantifiable from the disclosures reviewed)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: DV12 restatement: FCF-based reverse DCF after SBC at 10.4% (5.17% Treasury + 1.27 x 4.14%) implies 13.6% (FY27E FCF about $11.9bn) to 19.3% (TTM $7.8bn) 10-year growth versus a base of about 10%, so above; the earlier in_line call used non-GAAP EPS (SBC added back) and no discount rate. Verdict INCLUDE-SMALL -> WATCH; H1 FY27 cash conversion has fallen (OCF/NI 0.83x, Q2 FCF -47% YoY).

DELL.scenario_basis: DV12 restated on GAAP EPS: EPS0 = $24.37 (FY27 GAAP guide); EPS grown 5%/18%/30% a year for 2 more years to $26.9/$33.9/$41.2; exit P/E 12x/18x/22x; plus about $6.0/7.0/7.6 cumulative dividends; start $562.89; annualised over 3 years (the earlier non-GAAP basis gave -15.2%/+4.8%/+19.2%).

FIX.thesis_one_line: The leading mechanical/electrical contractor for data-center construction, with record backlog and margins, but priced for continued perfection with no margin of safety.
kill_criteria: Same-store backlog growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (vs +69% same-store at Q2-2026)
Technology/data-center segment revenue share falls below 45% of total revenue for two consecutive quarters (vs 58% at H1-2026)
Operating margin compresses by more than 200 bps YoY in any quarter (vs 17.1% at Q2-2026)
Net insider selling exceeds $100M in any rolling 6-month window with zero offsetting purchases (trailing-year run-rate already ~$152M)
Diluted EPS YoY growth falls below 15% for two consecutive quarters (vs 56-91% currently)
key_adverse_facts: The quant pipeline's TTM revenue ($3.96B) and TTM EBIT ($0.74B) inputs used in v4/outputs/v1_valuation.json are wrong by ~2.8x due to a filer XBRL tagging bug (FIX's Q1-2026 10-Q duplicate-tagged Q1-2025 quarterly figures with full-calendar-year-2025 date range); true TTM revenue is $11.23B and TTM EBIT is $1.85B (verified against the FY2025 10-K and each quarterly filing)
This data bug invalidates V1's FIX-specific reverse DCF (74.7% implied growth, -51.8%/yr base case, and the 'below Street target' flag are all artefacts of the bug, not real findings)

Heavy insider selling: CEO and CFO sold a combined ~$82M in Feb 2026 alone; ~$152M of insider sales over the trailing year with zero purchases (secondary-source Form 4 aggregation, not independently re-derived from each Form 4)
Revenue/backlog growth is concentrated in one end market (data-center/hyperscaler capex, now 58% of revenue vs 40% a year ago) - a genuine single-cycle dependency, not a diversified growth story
At 29.0x NTM P/E (73rd percentile of FIX's own 10-year history), even the corrected reverse DCF shows the market pricing in growth roughly at, not below, my own base case
data_conflicts: D3/V1 TTM revenue for FIX ($3,957,669,000) and TTM EBIT ($743,811,000) conflict with the primary-source 10-K/10-Q figures (TTM revenue $11,228,024,000 matching D4's Yahoo cross-check exactly; TTM EBIT $1,849,302,000), traced to an XBRL duplicate-context tagging bug in FIX's own Q1-2026 10-Q filing. All other V1 inputs for FIX (OCF, capex, SBC, net debt, shares, market cap, EV0, cost of capital, NTM P/E and its own-history percentile) were independently re-derived from the filings and matched V1 exactly.
FIX.confidence_in_thesis: high on the business-quality and data-conflict findings; medium on the WATCH-vs-INCLUDE-SMALL line, which is a close judgement call given a near-flat base-case return

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: I disagree with V1's 'excessive' verdict and its deeply negative scenario returns: they are built on a TTM revenue/EBIT input that is wrong by ~2.8x due to a filer XBRL tagging bug (see data_conflicts). V1's NTM P/E (29.0x), own-history percentile (73rd) and peer comparison are correct and unaffected. Recomputing V1's own reverse-DCF method with the corrected revenue/EBIT base implies ~11.6%/yr 10-year FCF growth priced in (vs V1's 74.7%), which is roughly in line with, not clearly below, my own base-case growth path - supporting 'fair', not 'excessive' or 'cheap'.

FIX.scenario_basis: TTM diluted EPS $40.64 (GAAP, FIX reports no non-GAAP measure); EPS grown to ~$49/$60/$70 (base), ~$49/$51/$54 (bear) or ~$50/$65/$85 (bull) over 3 years; exit P/E of 16x (bear)/24.4x (base, V1's own calibrated multiple)/29x (bull, current); plus ~$11 cumulative dividends; ~35.25M diluted shares.
